newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends limit-up, sentiment improves.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends limit-up, sentiment improves.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended limit-up in active trading on Monday with market sentiment improving after gains last Friday on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 20,950 yuan ($2,526) per tonne, rising 600 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 19,580 yuan per tonne.
August rose 440 to 20,540, September 410 to 20,670, October 570 to 20,920, December 580 to 20,940 and the January 1997 contract 530 to 20,380 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose sharply to 113,680 tonnes from 85,140.
Contracts opened higher but most at their intraday lows, with large amounts of buy orders pushing prices up steadily for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said market sentiment was much improved after Friday's LME gains and led to significant speculative buying on the Shanghai market on Monday.
The three months LME price broke above $2,300 per tonne, and by the end of the kerb was at $2,316, up $36 from Thursday.
London chartists said the copper market had been left open to further gains towards resistance at $2,360 a tonne on Monday.
"The LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai, with many investors believing copper would rise further in the next few days," one trader said.
"Heavy losses in the past few weeks created strong expectations of a powerful technical rebound," he said.
The benchmark November 1997 local contract opened at 20,580 yuan ($2,482) per tonne, up 230 yuan from Friday's close. It rose further early in the session.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices were around the 20,600 yuan level due to the sharp rebound on the futures market.
Traders said copper was likely to fluctuate sharply in the short term.
"Many speculators built positions in the past two trading days of price fluctuations," a second trader said.
"But heavy volume today indicated most investors expected further rises in the next few days," he said. "Any negative news will trigger large amounts of long liquidation."
Some traders said they expected copper to have a technical correction after the past two days of sharp rises.
Aluminium futures ended up in very dull trading.
August rose 370 to 13,770 and September 400 to 13,800 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 190 tonnes from 230 tonnes.
-- Shanghai Newsroom (8621) 6279-7004
